requirement:
`habeas add-input --item <file>:<line>` MUST parse the file under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` and add or refresh one
outline input for every outline node declared on that line. A named node is
declared on the line where its name begins in the source. An anonymous node, or
a named node whose name is not written in the source, such as an extern block
without an ABI string, is declared on the line where its own syntax starts,
excluding attached comments and attributes. Each input MUST store the selected `file` under the path
rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`, the node's selector, and its structural
hash. The command MUST report every selected node and reject a line on which no
node is declared.
rationale:
**Verdict: the requirement is met.** The implementation covers every obligation, it is marked `{impl}` throughout, and the tests cover the main cases and the failure cases.

**Implementation**
- **CLI.**
  - `Command::AddInput` in `src/main.rs` requires exactly one target (`--for-requirement` or `--for-example`) and exactly one mode (`--item` or `--requirements`).
  - `main` passes `--item <file>:<line>` to `add_input` as `InputMode::ItemsAtLine`.
- **Parsing under the outline requirement.** `selectors_for_mode` in `src/add_input.rs` splits the argument at the last `:` and requires a positive integer line. It parses the file with `OutlineCache::parse`, so a syntax error or a missing file is reported and rejected.
- **Every node declared on the line.** `Outline::declared_on_line` in `src/outline/mod.rs` returns all non-root nodes whose `declaration_line` equals the requested line, so nested or same-line nodes are all selected.
- **Declaration line rules.**
  - `Builder::walk` and `finish` compute `declaration_line`. A named node uses the byte where its name begins, which `name` returns as the start of the name field or child.
  - The custom naming rules return the name's start byte: `impl_name`, `extern_name`, CSS `selectors_name` and `prelude_name`, and Markdown `heading_name`.
  - An anonymous node, or a named node whose name is not written in the source, uses `child.start_byte()` of the core grammar node. Attached attributes and doc comments are stored separately and are not part of that start.
  - `extern_name` falls back to the node start when there is no ABI string.
  - Plain-text `line` nodes are declared on their own line.
- **Stored fields.**
  - `InputSelector::to_input` in `src/inputs.rs` writes exactly `file`, `item` and `hash`, with no source text.
  - `file` is made relative to the project when possible and kept absolute for allowed external sources, as the path rules require.
  - The hash is the node's structural hash.
- **Add or refresh.** `update_inputs` matches an existing outline input by selector. It reports `added`, `refreshed` or `unchanged` for each selected node and prints the selector in its output line. The same function also resets the review state and captures definitions. Other requirements specify that behaviour (`add_input`, `definitions.*`), and `update_inputs` carries `{impl}` markers for them.
- **Reject a line with no node.** `selectors_for_mode` returns `"<file>:<line>: no outline node is declared on this line"` for an empty selection. Nothing is written in that case.
- **Marking.** The `{impl}` markers cover the CLI, selection, resolution, input construction, outline declaration logic, and all custom naming functions. I found no unmarked code that implements part of the requirement.

**Tests**
- `src/outline/tests.rs::nodes_are_declared_on_their_name_line_or_where_their_syntax_starts` covers the declaration rule directly:
  - a wrapped Rust impl header;
  - an anonymous `use` after its doc comment and attribute;
  - extern blocks with and without an ABI string, including an ABI string on a later line;
  - Markdown headings;
  - a multi-line CSS `@media` with a nested rule.
- `add_input_item_selects_nodes_by_name_line_across_languages` covers:
  - a wrapped impl rejected on the `impl` line and accepted on its name line;
  - an anonymous `use` declared after its attribute;
  - a TOML pair and a Markdown section;
  - rejection of a blank line, line 0, a line past the end of the file, and a syntax-error file;
  - the record staying byte-identical after each rejection.
- `add_input_modes_capture_outline_nodes_and_refresh_idempotently` covers:
  - multiple nodes on one line (`fn[main]` and the nested `fn[main]/fn[nested]`);
  - plain-text line nodes;
  - repeat runs reporting `unchanged` and leaving the file byte-identical;
  - rejection of an attribute/comment line, a blank line, a non-numeric line and a missing file;
  - the hash ignoring the citation comment but including the doc comment.
- `add_input_requires_one_target_and_mode_and_resets_changed_records` covers argument validation and refresh of a changed source in place.
- `add_input_external_sources_respect_allow_and_disallow` covers absolute paths in `file` for allowed external sources and rejection of disallowed ones.

**Minor gap**
There are no per-line tests for the Python, TypeScript and YAML profiles. They use the generic `NameRule::Field` and `Anonymous` paths that the Rust, TOML, Markdown and CSS tests already exercise, so I don't treat this as a gap.

text: :::{req} add_input_item
`habeas add-input --item <file>:<line>` MUST parse the file under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` and add or refresh one
outline input for every outline node declared on that line. A named node is
declared on the line where its name begins in the source. An anonymous node, or
a named node whose name is not written in the source, such as an extern block
without an ABI string, is declared on the line where its own syntax starts,
excluding attached comments and attributes. Each input MUST store the selected `file` under the path
rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`, the node's selector, and its structural
hash. The command MUST report every selected node and reject a line on which no
node is declared.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. A source with any syntax error MUST fail to parse, reporting
the line of its first error. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
:::{req} schema

A requirement or example evidence file at `evidence/<full-name>.json` MUST be a JSON object with exactly `requirement` or `example`, `determination`, `rationale`, and `inputs`. The definition text and rationale MUST be nonempty strings, `determination` MUST use one of the outcomes defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`, and `inputs` MUST be an array. Every evidence input MUST have exactly one of three forms: an outline input with `file`, `item`, and `hash`; a requirements input with `requirements`, `matches`, and `text`; or a definition input with `definition` and `text`. File paths MUST resolve to permitted inputs under {cite}`requirements.ci.input_containment`. Project-local paths SHOULD be recorded relative to the project for portability; absolute and parent-relative paths MAY be used when their resolved targets are permitted. `matches` MUST be an array of distinct full definition names, `hash` MUST be a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest, and `text` MUST be a nonempty array of strings. Evidence MUST NOT store source text for outline inputs.
